summary: A Delphi-based Windows desktop application for parsing, evaluating, and visualizing mathematical expressions, developed as an academic coursework project following BSUIR standards.
key_features: Custom mathematical expression parser with lexical and syntactic analysis
Real-time evaluation engine with operator precedence and error handling
Interactive graphical visualization with scrolling, scaling, and coordinate mapping
Native VCL-based Windows GUI for input and configuration
Comprehensive academic documentation with algorithm flowcharts and BSUIR-compliant LaTeX templates
achievements: Designed and implemented a custom expression parser and evaluation engine from scratch, successfully handling operator precedence, parentheses, variables, and runtime errors. Developed a custom graphical rendering system for mathematical fields with interactive coordinate transformation, scrolling, and scaling. Built a standalone test harness for isolated parser validation and structured the full development lifecycle with GOST-compliant documentation and algorithm flowcharts.
